# loam protection matrix — failure mode × guard

loam's *protection pillar* (doctrine §"The two sides of leg 2 — translation in, protection around"): each known way an AI betrays a user by default, loam's actual guard against it, whether that guard is on by default for everyone, whether the failure mode is **floor-class** (non-negotiable) or **proportional**, and how we verify the guard fires.

This page is generated from the machine-checkable catalogue and reflects the live coverage verdict as of the date below. The **gaps** — floor-class failure modes guarded today only by persona discipline — are the actionable output, not a defect to hide.

*Coverage checked: 2026-05-31. 6 floor-class gap(s) open.*

## The matrix

| Failure mode | Guard | Kind | Class | Default-on | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FM.HALLUCINATION** — Invents things that do not exist | information-trust-ordering + claim-or-cite discipline + the substrate-audit comparator (catches a shipping doc's stale status claim) | comparator | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.MISSING-CONTEXT** — Works from missing or degraded context | SessionStart corpus-load gate (loads the operating corpus at session start) + the precompact reinject skill (re-asserts discipline across compaction) | hook | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.SILENT-BREAKAGE** — One change breaks the surrounding work | ODD objective-binding gate + TDD guard + the pre-publish release-gate chain | hook | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.GOAL-DRIFT** — Loses the original goal | ODD authoring (every line maps to a named AC) + the active-scope sentinel hook | hook | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.NO-MEMORY** — Has no real memory | file-based memory (the FBM corpus) + the loam-memory-inspect tooling over it | memory | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.NARRATION-NOT-ACTION** — Narrates intent without taking the action | persona-discipline only — the channel auto-route fix closed ONE hole (un-replied conversational text); no general programmatic guard that a work-turn ends on a work/reply tool call | persona-discipline | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.INFERRED-RHYTHM** — Infers the user's session, time, or rhythm | persona-discipline only | persona-discipline | proportional | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | — |
| **FM.ENV-PERCEPTION-MVC** — Confuses its internal env-model with the user's view | persona-discipline only | persona-discipline | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.PROCESS-DRIFT-UNDER-PRESSURE** — Abandons the defined flow under pressure | the keep-pace flow-position hooks (partial — they re-assert flow position) + mostly persona-discipline | persona-discipline | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.BUILT-NE-LIVE** — Claims built/published from prose, not git refs | the substrate-audit gate (catches a shipping DOC claiming a live component is dark / vice-versa) — partial: shipping docs only, not arbitrary in-conversation claims | release-gate | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.STALE-MEMORY-VS-TRUTH** — Trusts a stored claim over live ground truth | the FBM reconcile entry-point — the SAME comparator the doc-audit uses, routing a stored claim through compare_claim for checkable claims | comparator | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.SECRET-LEAK** — Commits secrets or .env files | the secret-pattern guard hook + the dangerous-flag guard hook | hook | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.DESTRUCTIVE-PRUNE** — Deletes a load-bearing thing while pruning | the reversibility primitive (every prune tracked in version control, rollback-able) + the surface-before-destructive discipline + the depends-on-it check (partial — reversibility is programmatic, the depends-on check is persona-discipline) | persona-discipline | floor | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | **YES** |
| **FM.BOUNDARY-VIOLATION** — Framework writes user-state outside its declared homes | the boundary-respected release gate | release-gate | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.MIGRATION-GAP** — Ships a state change with no migration | the migration-declared release gate | release-gate | floor | YES | — |
| **FM.FALSE-FAULT** — Manufactures a fault that isn't real | persona-discipline only — the four-test discipline before writing an audit ✗ | persona-discipline | proportional | NO-PROGRAMMATIC | — |

## The gaps (floor-class, no default-on guard)

Each of these floor-class failure modes is today guarded only by persona discipline (or partially) — a prose rule the doctrine itself says "decays first under pressure." Each is a structural-enforcement candidate (`feedback_structural_enforcement_on_recurrence`):

### FM.HALLUCINATION — Invents things that do not exist

- **Betrayal:** Confidently states facts, sources, counts, or statuses it has not verified — the canonical AI betrayal (doctrine: "inventing things that do not exist").
- **Today's guard:** information-trust-ordering + claim-or-cite discipline + the substrate-audit comparator (catches a shipping doc's stale status claim)
- **Source:** docs/design/loam-doctrine.md §two-sides-of-leg-2; feedback_information_trust_ordering.md; feedback_claim_or_cite_no_fake_sources.md
- **Why it's a gap:** The comparator IS exercised on shipping docs at publish (check_substrate_audit); but broad fact-recall has no programmatic check — the comparator covers status-claim drift only, persona discipline covers the rest. PARTIAL coverage → floor gap on non-doc claims.

### FM.NARRATION-NOT-ACTION — Narrates intent without taking the action

- **Betrayal:** Says it will do the work (or claims it did) without ever emitting the tool call — terminal-only intent-text the user never sees as a result.
- **Today's guard:** persona-discipline only — the channel auto-route fix closed ONE hole (un-replied conversational text); no general programmatic guard that a work-turn ends on a work/reply tool call
- **Source:** feedback_narration_is_not_action.md (born from the 2026-05-31 silent-night failure; fired four times in one night)
- **Why it's a gap:** UNVERIFIABLE by a deterministic check — a prose rule the doctrine itself says "decays first under pressure." This is a GAP: the recurrence (four fires in one night despite the corpus rule) is the structural-enforcement trigger (feedback_structural_enforcement_on_recurrence).

### FM.ENV-PERCEPTION-MVC — Confuses its internal env-model with the user's view

- **Betrayal:** Treats its own model of the environment (files, state, what's on screen) as what the user actually sees — a model/view confusion.
- **Today's guard:** persona-discipline only
- **Source:** feedback_environment_perception_model_dont_assume.md (explicitly the THIRD instance in one session)
- **Why it's a gap:** UNVERIFIABLE by a deterministic check. This is a GAP — a floor-class betrayal guarded only by a prose rule that has already recurred (third instance in one session).

### FM.PROCESS-DRIFT-UNDER-PRESSURE — Abandons the defined flow under pressure

- **Betrayal:** Drops the structured flow it was following when the work gets hard or urgent — exactly when the flow matters most (doctrine: "a defined flow decays first under pressure").
- **Today's guard:** the keep-pace flow-position hooks (partial — they re-assert flow position) + mostly persona-discipline
- **Source:** docs/design/loam-doctrine.md §Follow-the-defined-workflow; feedback_defined_workflow_in_context_pause_if_lost.md
- **Why it's a gap:** PARTIAL: keep-pace re-asserts flow position (framework/hands-off-lifecycle/hooks/keep_pace/), but there is no programmatic guard that the flow is actually FOLLOWED under pressure. Floor gap — the residual is persona discipline.

### FM.BUILT-NE-LIVE — Claims built/published from prose, not git refs

- **Betrayal:** Reports a thing as built/sealed/merged/published from a status line or a prior agent's summary rather than the git ref graph — stale-prone Tier-2 prose treated as ground truth.
- **Today's guard:** the substrate-audit gate (catches a shipping DOC claiming a live component is dark / vice-versa) — partial: shipping docs only, not arbitrary in-conversation claims
- **Source:** feedback_published_state_only_from_git_refs.md
- **Why it's a gap:** The substrate-audit gate IS wired into ALL_GATES + runs at publish against shipping docs (real, default-on for THAT surface). But a built/published CLAIM made in conversation (not in an audited doc) has no programmatic check → PARTIAL → floor gap for non-doc claims.

### FM.DESTRUCTIVE-PRUNE — Deletes a load-bearing thing while pruning

- **Betrayal:** Cuts a "vestigial" rule or compresses a sentence that was actually load-bearing — the pruning leg's signature betrayal (doctrine: "a confident hallucination with a delete key").
- **Today's guard:** the reversibility primitive (every prune tracked in version control, rollback-able) + the surface-before-destructive discipline + the depends-on-it check (partial — reversibility is programmatic, the depends-on check is persona-discipline)
- **Source:** docs/design/loam-doctrine.md §pruning (every prune reversible + destructive cuts surfaced before they happen + check 'does anything still depend on it?')
- **Why it's a gap:** PARTIAL: the reversibility primitive (framework/reversibility-primitive/) makes prunes rollback-able (real, programmatic), but "does anything still depend on it?" + the surface-before-cut step are persona discipline → floor gap on the decision-to-cut, covered programmatically only on the undo side.
